articleTitle: Aberration analysis in diffration imaging of a small Kepler-type double-lens optical system
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: a small Kepler-type double-lens optical system is constructed by using Zemax, based on Kirchhoff diffraction theory, the aberration function is introduced into the electric filed of Gaussion beam by using Zernike polynomial, and the aberration is analysed in diffration imaging of the optical system by using Zemax and MATLAB. We find the simulation results by Zemax are highly consistent with the numerical results of MATLAB in the constructed optical system, and the quadrafoil aberration is produced in diffration imaging. However, by adopting Zernike standard high-vector convex mirror as aberration compensation plate, and optimizing the lens material, curvature radius and thickness in the system, the quadrafoil aberration can be effectively controled, the effect of wavelength on imaging quality can be reduced, the wavelength range of effective imaging can be expanded, and enhance the overall imaging quality of the system.

articleTitle: Dual-function terahertz ultra-broadband modulator based on the vanadium dioxide and gold
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a dual-functional terahertz metasurface based on vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Within the same frequency range, it seamlessly transitions between functioning as a wideband absorber and a reflective wideband linear-to-cross (LTX) polarization converter. This metasurface design offers numerous advantages, including functional versatility, a substantial relative bandwidth, and an expanded operational range for incident angles and polarization orientations. In its metallic phase, VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> enables the multifunctional metasurface to achieve absorption rates exceeding 90% within the 1.11-3.36 THz frequency range. The bandwidth and relative bandwidth are 2.25 THz and 100.7%, respectively. We analyze the underlying principles of the absorption effect using surface current images and impedance matching theory. In its insulating phase, a polarization conversion efficiency exceeding 90% within the 0.86-2.25 THz frequency range is facilitated by VO2, with a relative bandwidth of 89.4%. Moreover, it functions as a half-wave plate. In its insulating phase, a polarization conversion efficiency exceeding 90% within the 0.86-2.25 THz frequency range is facilitated by VO2, with a relative bandwidth of 89.4%. Moreover, it functions as a half-wave plate. This research has expanded its operational bandwidth and endowed it with additional functionalities. The proposed dual-functional terahertz modulator has the characteristics of a large relative bandwidth, simple structure, and high process feasibility, which makes it potentially useful in terahertz detection, modulation, and switching fields.

articleTitle: Monitoring the curing process of polyurethane materials based on terahertz technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: Polyurethane materials possess excellent insulation, heat resistance, and durability, making them excellent adhesives for composite structural materials in high-temperature and high-pressure environments. The quality of adhesion at the interface is closely related to its curing state. Therefore, non-contact monitoring of the transition from the liquid to solid state prevents issues like weak bonding at the adhesive interface, significantly enhancing the adhesion quality and safety of composite structural materials. Such monitoring finds extensive applications in various fields, including aerospace, energy, and power, among others. In this study, the reflection-mode terahertz time-domain spectroscopy technique was employed to monitor the curing reaction process of polyurethane materials. Additionally, refractive index spectra of samples at different curing times were extracted, and the relationship between the refractive index and curing reaction time was established. Furthermore, a comparison was made with the material loss factor obtained through a rheometer to determine the correlation between the refractive index and the material loss factor. The experimental results indicate that during the curing process, the refractive index demonstrates a gradual decrease and stabilizes after 225 minutes of curing. The correlation coefficient between the refractive index and the material loss factor exceeds 0.9. As the curing reaction progresses, the refractive index accurately reflects the curing process of polyurethane materials. This study provides an effective means for monitoring the curing process of polyurethane materials.

articleTitle: PXI-based measurement and analysis of 230-330 GHz terahertz vertical wall reflection channels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: The emergence of terahertz technology defines the future of mobile communications, which has the potential to unleash the full capabilities of sixth generation networks, the key to which is the exploration of terahertz wireless channels as the basis for terahertz communications. In this paper, based on the introduction of the measurement method of reflection characteristics of indoor wireless channel, based on the vector signal transceiver platform PXI, the reflection measurements of vertical incidence angle, vertical reception of three materials, namely, stainless steel brushed, stainless steel unbrushed and white paper, in 230~330GHz frequency band in indoor environment are conducted, and the relationship between the reflection distance and the path loss is analysed. The experimental results show that the reflection loss shows a tendency of decreasing and then becoming larger as the distance increases, and the reflection loss is related to the roughness of the reflecting surface of the material. Finally, an outlook on the study of terahertz channel reflection characteristics is given.

articleTitle: Enhancement effect of terahertz wave security inspection images by combining large threshold value mean filtering with Canny algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: Owing to its non-damage property and noninvasive detection, terahertz waves have broad application prospects in the field of human safety detection. However, due to the limitation of the resolution of the terahertz wave itself and the interference of the external environment, the passive terahertz human safety imaging system obtains the initial terahertz wave human body image with high noise, resulting in poor image contrast, blurred boundaries and cannot be directly recognized by the machine. How to improve the image quality and resolution of terahertz human body and hidden objects has become a key problem in terahertz human safety imaging research. In this paper, we employed a passive terahertz wave human body security inspection imaging system to image the human body and hidden objects. An algorithm combining mean filtering of large threshold values with canny is proposed to improve the quality of the passive terahertz wave human security inspection image. The image is denoising through large threshold values mean filtering, and the Canny algorithm is used to obtain the clear edge of the human body and hidden objects, and retain and highlight the terahertz image details of the human body and hidden objects. The experimental results show that the combination of large threshold values mean filtering and Canny algorithm has a good noise reduction effect on terahertz images, which will let the images have clear details and high contrast, and make them suitable for passive terahertz human body security imaging system.

articleTitle: Terahertz broadband absorption and phonon dispersion of gallium telluride
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: The III-VI group layered metal chalcogenides Gallium telluride (GaTe) has attracted a lot interests due to its unique band gap and crystal structure. We investigate the terahertz broadband absorption of GaTe in the range of 0-25 THz, by a terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) system with two-color air plasma broadband terahertz generation and air-biased coherent detection (ABCD). The dielectric function and the phonon dispersion of GaTe in this broad terahertz frequency range is studied to understand the optical and thermal properties of GaTe.

articleTitle: Quasi-Bound States in the Continuum in Terahertz Trimer-Based Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are waves confined localized with an infinite quality (Q) factor and zero bandwidth resonance in the frequency spectrum, and quasiBICs preserves their high Q-factor characteristics with limited resonance bandwidth which facilitates observation. Here, we propose a method utilizing terahertz trimer-based metamaterials to generate different numbers of quasi-BICs via changing the spacings between the primitive unit structures while keeping their geometric parameters consistent, and we discuss the relation between the number of equal spacings and the number of quasi-BICs. We prove that 0, 1 and 2 quasi-BICs could be generated when 0, 2 and 3 spacings of all the three spacings in the trimer are unequal, respectively. We also discuss the relevance of quasi-BICs generated in different cases that all the three spacings are unequal and only two spacings are equal.

articleTitle: Backward THz emission from two-color laser field-induced gas plasma
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: Two-color laser field-induced plasma filament is an efficient broadband terahertz (THz) source with intense THz waves emitted mainly in the forward direction and has been investigated intensively. However, investigations on the backward emission from such a THz source are rather rare. Recently, we theoretically and experimentally investigate the backward THz wave radiation from two-color laser field-induced plasma filament. In theory, a linear dipole array model predicts that THz waves can be emitted in both the forward and backward direction from plasma filaments with different lengths. However, the proportion of backward emitted THz wave decreases with the length of the plasma filament. In experiment, we obtain the typical waveform and spectrum of the backward THz radiation from a plasma with a length of about 5 mm. The electric field of the backward THz wave is about two or three orders of magnitude lower than that of the forward THz wave while the major frequency components of the backward THz spectrum are below 1 THz, which can be attributed to the destructive interference of THz waves, emitted from local dipoles created at different time and positions along plasma, in the backward direction. Our investigation on the dependence of the peak THz amplitude on the laser pulse energy implies that the THz generation processes of the forward and backward THz waves are essentially the same. As the laser pulse energy changes, there is a peak timing shift in the backward THz waveform, implying a plasma position change caused by the nonlinear-focusing effect. The sensitivity to the plasma position of the backward THz wave may have potential applications in the fields of THz imaging and remote sensing. Our work could contribute to further understanding THz emission process, and may help to develop potential applications of the THz source based on two-color laser-induce plasma filament.

articleTitle: Circuit design of AC-powered glow discharge terahertz wave detector
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: The glow discharge detector (GDD), which is based on the plasma generated by glow discharge to detect terahertz (THz) waves, has the advantages of fast response, small noise equivalent power, the ability to work at room temperature, and low price, which makes it a new type of THz detector with a good prospect. In this paper, different circuit parameters were tested under DC power supply to find out the best combination of resistance and capacitance values. GDDs of different sizes and GDDs with or without a phosphorescent layer were tested, and the effects of these factors on the responsivity of GDDs were analyzed. Based on the traditional circuit using DC power supply, the AC-powered detection method was proposed, and the unipolar modulation and bipolar modulation power supply circuit were designed, and THz signals were successfully obtained. This work pave a new way to enhance the detection performance of GDD.

articleTitle: The simulation of beam arrival time jitter of THz source based on superconducting accelerators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: China Academy of Engineering Physics Terahertz Free Electron Laser (CAEP THz FEL, CTFEL) is the first high-average power free electron laser terahertz user source based on superconducting accelerators in China. It has some characteristics such as high repetition (54.167MHz), high average power (>10W), and continuously adjustable frequency (0.7THz to 4.2THz). One of the critical issues of the user THz source is the time jitter. The jitter of the electron beam arrival time has a massive influence on the total time jitter in the experimental station. In order to study the ultrafast dynamic process in CTFEL with some techniques, such as pump-probe, SNOM, and single-pulse detection, an accurate beam arrival time jitter analysis in the beam line is needed. A program named a space charge tracking algorithm (ASTRA) is used to simulate the electron beam dynamic and calculate the beam arrival time at the entrance of the undulator in CTFEL. All the parameters in the simulation are from the experimental data of the facility. The simulation results show that the RMS arrival time jitter before the optical cavity is about 728 fs, and the significant contribution to arrival time jitter is the amplitude fluctuation of RF fields of two boosters in the superconducting accelerators, more than 95%.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Investigation for Pair-Breaking in Superconducting States under Terahertz Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: By solving the superconducting states and nonlinear Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) equations, we study the strongly coupled electron-photon system and investigate the nonlinear response of superconducting gap, carriers and supercurrent made by niobium nitride (NbN) at various parameters $\frac{E}{\omega }$, temperature and energy gap. In this model, Cooper-pair will be broken due to multi-photons absorptions even if the photon energy is smaller than the superconducting gap. Our analysis calculates the electron state under intense fields, and the equation of superconducting gap. As the parameter $\frac{E}{\omega }$ changes, an obvious modulation is observed due to the strong nonlinear effect. It shows that the critical temperature is influenced by $\frac{E}{\omega }$, which was distinct from that induced by the heating effect. The energy gap, superconducting carriers and supercurrent also were affected which accords with the experiments. In the linear region, Cooper pairs are destroyed by absorption photons while energies are higher than the energy gap, the absorption rate is independent on the field. In the nonlinear region, the low-frequency field will suppress the superconducting state. Physical mechanism mainly relies on the multi-photon absorption process of superconducting electrons. Nonlinear absorption will occur under an intense field interaction, and the number of absorption photon is proportional to the n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> power of the electric field strength. The energy gap is dependent on the electric field, which indicates the superconducting state can be suppressed under a strong field at low frequencies. In addition, nonlinear absorption process could reduce the gap width and the critical temperature, but due to the rate of nonlinear absorption is hard to reach 100%, the energy gap cannot be closed completely under a strong field, which is different from the critical temperature.

articleTitle: Research on optical properties of human hepatoma cells using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: Terahertz technology is a non-invasive and label-free inspection method, promising for applications in various fields, especially in biomedical diagnosis. Terahertz radiation is capable for cell physiological and pathological status recognition due to its sensitivity to cell composition and structural information of biomacromolecular. In this paper, the transmission properties of glass, polymethyl methacrylate and polypropylene in THz regime were compared and polypropylene was selected as the petri dish material for cell adhesion due to its high transmission of terahertz wave. The time-domain and frequency-domain spectra, refractive index and absorption coefficient of hepatoma cell line Huh7 and normal cell line MIHA were analyzed. The experimental results showed significant distinction between the terahertz characteristic spectra of hepatoma cells and normal cells. This work can be helpful for applying terahertz technology in cancer detection at the cellular level.

articleTitle: A 2.4 GHz Fully Integrated, 50-Ohm Matched Power Amplifier for Bluetooth Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: A 2.4 GHz power amplifier (PA) for Bluetooth application is designed in TSMC 0.18 um RF CMOS process using Advanced Design System from Keysight. Across the operating frequency range of 2.4 GHz to 2.483 GHz, the PA exhibits a 12 dB gain with less than 0.5 dB fluctuation. At the center frequency of 2.44 GHz, the PA presents a maximum output power of 18 dBm with a corresponding PAE of 50%. Under the output power from -20 dBm to 15 dBm, this PA shows better than 22.5 dBm OIP3. The proposed PA is fully integrated and 50-Ohm matched, which can directly fit into the RF front-end system.

articleTitle: A method to detect gas based on the Fabry–Pérot cavity by using terahertz frequency-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: Due to the limitation of the gas volume as well as the optical path, sometimes the absorption peak of the gas is difficult to observe. Here, we present a new gas detection method based on the Fabry–Pérot cavity, which can effectively enhance the absorption peaks of gases by using terahertz frequency-domain spectroscopy. By changing the cavity length, the cavity resonance center frequency and resonance modes can be changed to detect multiple gases or to observe the performance of the same gas in different resonance modes. The enhancement of the absorption peak at 560 GHz for water vapor has been successfully observed, and it is expected to be useful for the detection of various substances.

articleTitle: AlGaN/GaN HEMT Sub-Terahertz Detectors Integrated with Spiral Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Ultrafast Phenomena and Terahertz Waves (ISUPTW)
abstract: This paper presents a study of an AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) terahertz detector integrated with a planar spiral antenna. The proposed device is designed to operate in the backward wave oscillator (BWO) fundamental frequency range of 175-385 GHz, which is important for various applications such as security checking, medical imaging, and communications. The spiral antenna is used to efficiently couple THz radiation into the detector, and the AlGaN/GaN HEMT is used as the sensing element. The proposed device was designed and simulated using commercial software Comsol and Silvaco TCAD. The simulation results show that the device has the maximum responsivity of 2197.5 V/W at 208 GHz, and exhibit good absorption rates at 206-211 GHz and 296-299 GHz. Optimizing the integration method by transitioning from source-drain integration to gate-source integration enhances the asymmetry of detector, thereby improving responsivity to 3500 V/W and increasing bandwidth to 230-255, 285-305 and 360-385 GHz, the multi-band response characteristic is mainly attributed to the specially designed spiral antenna. In addition, the effects of antenna size and shape on the device performance were investigated through simulation. It was found that the spiral structure provides better performance compared to the bow-tie structure in our previous work, and increasing the antenna size can improve the characteristics of responsivity and noise equivalent power (NEP). The proposed device has the potential to be a promising candidate for future THz sensing applications due to its high responsivity, broad bandwidth, low NEP, good linearity and compact size.
